adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated=false, dropping the isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check so Mimir federated rules become editable/deletable in the legacy list and details views

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (deprecated wrapper), and `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO, removing the prior `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`-based immutability check. As a result, federated rule groups will no longer be marked immutable via the `immutableRule` flag, potentially enabling Update/Delete actions when `useIsRuleEditable(...)` returns true. This is a real behavior change grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — Pause stays gated on rulerRule, which the list view no longer provides, so Pause/Resume can never appear in the list even when prom abilities grant it (regression vs the old ruler-backed list)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly updates `AlertRuleMenu` to check Pause (and other actions) against *both* ruler-based abilities and Grafana Prom rule abilities. It calls `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...)`, then computes `canPause` as `(pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`. Additionally, `useRulerRuleAbilities` was changed to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`, so list-view absence of `rulerRule` does not inherently gate Pause. The finding claims Pause remains gated only on `rulerRule`, which is contradicted by the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — Delete stays gated on rulerRule, so the list view loses Delete even for users with folder delete permission because canDelete from the prom path is ignored

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff explicitly adds a Prom-rule ability path via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...) and combines it with the ruler path using logical OR. For delete: `const [deleteSupported, deleteAllowed] = rulerDeleteAbility; const [grafanaDeleteSupported, grafanaDeleteAllowed] = grafanaDeleteAbility; const canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed);` so delete is not gated solely on `rulerRule` and the Prom/folder-permission path is not ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:207 — The test grants update/delete permissions yet asserts exactly 4 menu items, which locks in the missing Pause/Delete regression, and it never clicks Silence so the no-op drawer goes green

public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:324 — The prom path limits ModifyExport/Pause/Restore to isAlertingRule, but the ruler path allowed every Grafana-managed rule, so Grafana recording rules lose Export/Pause in the list view

adjudication.rationale: In useAbilities.ts, the new prom-based abilities hook (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) gates ModifyExport/Pause/Restore on `isAlertingRule` (derived from `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`), whereas the existing ruler-based path (useAllRulerRuleAbilities) gates those actions on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (i.e., any Grafana-managed rule, including recording rules). The diff also changes list rendering to rely on Prometheus rules only (GrafanaGroupLoader now maps `promResponse...rules` and GrafanaRuleListItem always renders `RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule}`), so recording rules in the list view will now compute abilities via the prom path and lose ModifyExport/Pause/Restore compared to the ruler path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:83 — ORing ruler and prom abilities resolves disagreements permissively: when the ruler denies (provisioned via grafana_alert.provenance, or ruler still loading) but the prom path allows (the new optional provenance field is absent, or AlwaysSupported), Pause/Delete/Duplicate show on immutable rules wherever both rules are passed

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the ability gates for Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export are now computed as an OR between the ruler-derived ability and the GrafanaPromRule-derived ability (e.g., `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`). The new GrafanaPromRule path (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts) determines immutability via `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which depends on `promRule.provenance`, but `provenance` was added as an optional field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` (`provenance?: string`). If a rule is provisioned on the ruler side (and thus should be immutable) but the prom DTO lacks `provenance`, the prom abilities will treat it as mutable and can allow actions based on folder permissions, causing the OR to surface actions that the ruler path would deny. This is a correctness regression enabled by the diff’s new permissive OR-combination and the optional provenance signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40 — The rule view href no longer includes returnTo (the old code used createReturnTo()), so navigating back from a rule loses the user's filtered list state

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx, GrafanaRuleListItem built the view link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, preserving a returnTo query param for navigation back to the filtered list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx now sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo, and FilterView was changed to render GrafanaRuleListItem directly. This diff-groundedly removes propagation of returnTo from the list to the rule view, plausibly breaking “back to list with same filter state” behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:68 — With the ruler/prom reconciliation and Creating/Deleting states removed, a rule already deleted in the ruler but still in prom shows live Edit/More actions that point to a 404, and a just-created rule is invisible until prom catches up

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx the PR removes the ruler query and the prom/ruler reconciliation (matchRules, promOnlyRules, and the Creating/Deleting list items) and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem`s. This means a rule that exists only in the ruler (previously rendered with `RuleOperation.Creating`) will no longer be shown at all until it appears in the Prom response, and a rule that exists only in Prom (previously rendered as a `RuleOperationListItem` with Deleting and no actions) will now be rendered as a normal rule with `RuleActionsButtons` (Edit/More) via `GrafanaRuleListItem`. The diff therefore directly removes the protective UI states the finding describes, exposing the listed behaviors if the two sources are ever temporarily out of sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:213 — The automocked ability hooks ignore their rule argument, so the skipToken gating and the real OR permission logic are never exercised and the tests pass whatever the prom-path behavior is

adjudication.rationale: In RulesTable.test.tsx the mocked implementations for the new plural hooks (e.g., useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities.mockImplementation((_rule, actions) => actions.map(() => [false,false])) and per-test overrides) ignore the first argument entirely. That means the production behavior added in this diff—passing skipToken from AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons when the prom rule isn’t a Grafana prom rule (AlertRuleMenu.tsx uses `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`)—is not exercised/validated by tests because the mock will return the same abilities regardless of whether the component passes a real rule or skipToken. Similarly, most test setups make both sides of the new OR logic align (both allow/deny), so they don’t specifically validate the intended “ruler OR prom” permission behavior. This is a test coverage/mocking fidelity issue, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — Silence menu item is now shown via prom abilities in the list view (rule is undefined), but the drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, so clicking "Silence notifications" does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` now renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` (`<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />`), meaning `rule` (the `RulerRuleDTO`) can be `undefined`. At the same time, `AlertRuleMenu` was changed to compute abilities using both ruler abilities and Grafana Prom rule abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...promRule...)`), so the Silence action can be considered allowed and therefore shown even when no `rulerRule` exists. If `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` still gates the silence drawer rendering on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (as the finding states), then with `rule === undefined` the drawer would never render, making the displayed “Silence notifications” action non-functional in this list-view scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — Delete (and Pause at line 123) menu items are still gated on `rulerRule` being present, so the newly computed prom-based delete/pause abilities are dead code and Grafana rules in the list view lose Delete and Pause actions

adjudication.rationale: The diff chunk for `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` only shows ability computation refactored to OR together `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` results (e.g., `canPause`, `canDelete`). It does not include the later JSX where menu items are rendered, so the claim that Delete/Pause menu items are still gated on `rulerRule` being present (making the prom-based abilities dead code) cannot be verified from the provided diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:73 — With skipToken (non-Grafana promRule), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns Duplicate as [AlwaysSupported, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)], and OR-ing this into canDuplicate shows Duplicate for data-source rules even when the ruler is unavailable or the user lacks external write permission

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the Grafana prom-rule abilities are always OR-ed into the final booleans (e.g. canDuplicate), and the hook is invoked even when the rule is not a Grafana prom rule by passing `skipToken` (which becomes `undefined`) to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(), when `rule` is undefined, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`, `immutableRule` is false, and `Duplicate` support becomes `AlwaysSupported` (via `duplicateSupported = ... ? NotSupported : MaybeSupported`) with allowance based only on Grafana create permission (`getRulesPermissions('grafana')`). That means a non-Grafana (datasource) rule can incorrectly get `grafanaDuplicateAbility` as supported/allowed and make `canDuplicate` true even if the ruler ability is not supported/allowed for that rule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated=false, dropping the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check so federated Mimir rules become editable/deletable in the legacy list and details views

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s claim that Delete/Pause are missing because AlertRuleMenu “still requires rulerRule” is contradicted by the diff: AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler abilities with Grafana Prom rule abilities via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/promRule (with skipToken) for Pause/Delete/etc. However, the test in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx grants delete/update permissions (grantUserPermissions + setFolderAccessControl) yet asserts exactly 4 menuitems after clicking “More” and never asserts the defined ui.menuItems.delete(). Given the new ability plumbing, Delete (and possibly Pause) may legitimately appear, making the hard-coded `menuItems.length === 4` expectation fragile/incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:221 — Fixture rulerRuleToPromRule never sets provenance and there are no plugin/recording variants, so isProvisionedPromRule (utils/rules.ts:171) and the provisioned/immutable path (hide Edit, block Pause/Delete) added by this PR are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The PR introduces new “provisioned/immutable” behavior for Grafana Prom rules via `provenance` (added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` in `public/app/types/unified-alerting-dto.ts`) and `isProvisionedPromRule()` (new in `public/app/features/alerting/unified/utils/rules.ts`). That provisioned flag is then used to disable abilities in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` (in `useAbilities.ts`, `immutableRule` -> `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`) and to mark list items as provisioned in `GrafanaRuleListItem` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2` (`getIsProvisioned()` falls back to `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)`). The updated/added tests in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` and `RulesTable.test.tsx` exercise permission-based enable/disable paths, but do not show any scenario where a Grafana prom rule has `provenance` set (nor plugin-provided/recording variants), so the new provisioned/immutable paths remain untested. The finding’s specific reference to a `rulerRuleToPromRule` fixture is not verifiable from this diff (that code was removed from the test file), but the underlying “new provisioned path is untested” concern is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:165 — The negative Edit-button check runs right after the rule item appears, but useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns isEditable=false while the folder loads, so the test can pass without ever exercising the permission denial.

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the new test `should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions` waits for the rule list item to appear (`ui.ruleItem(...).find()`) and then immediately asserts the Edit button is absent. In the diff, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` relies on `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()`, which returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false }` when the folder is not yet loaded (`if (!folder) { ... isEditable: false ... loading }`). That means the Edit button can be absent transiently due to folder-loading, so the negative assertion can pass without actually validating the permission-denial path (i.e., it may never reach the post-folder-load state). This is a test robustness issue, not necessarily a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:68 — New promRule-only branches (getEditableIdentifier returning undefined, which logs a warning and renders null; getIsProvisioned via promRule; OR-combined edit ability) have no targeted tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new promRule-only logic in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (e.g., `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, `getEditableIdentifier`, and the OR-combined `canEditRule`). However, the PR also adds/updates tests that exercise the promRule-only rendering path where `RuleActionsButtons` is fed only a `promRule`: `GrafanaRuleListItem` now passes `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />`, and `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` asserts Edit button presence/absence based on permissions and checks the Edit href for multiple rules. That provides targeted coverage of the promRule-only identifier construction and edit-ability decision. While the defensive branch where `getEditableIdentifier` returns `undefined` (logging and returning `null`) is not explicitly tested, the finding’s blanket claim that the new promRule-only branches have no targeted tests is not supported by the diff.
